title: Approximation transfer from three-literal SAT
statement: Let $V$ be a finite set of variables, let $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0\leq\delta$, and let $A$ be an algorithm that assigns Boolean values to variables for every three-literal satisfiability instance over $V$. Suppose that on every such instance $Q$, if its optimum satisfied fraction is at least $1-\delta$, then $A(Q)$ satisfies a fraction at least $7/8+\delta$. Then, for every three-variable linear constraint instance $P$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$ on $V$, if its optimum satisfied fraction is at least $1-\delta$, the assignment produced by applying $A$ to the associated three-literal instance and interpreting its Boolean values in $\mathbb{F}_2$ satisfies a fraction at least $1/2+\delta$ of the constraints of $P$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ maps each three-literal satisfiability instance on $V$ to a Boolean assignment on $V$
